title: Sharjah Criterion: A Two-Stage Empirical Lunar Crescent Visibility Model
description: A data-driven two-stage logistic-regression criterion for lunar crescent visibility, derived from the crescent sighting reports of the Islamic Crescents' Observation Project (ICOP). The pipeline scrapes, cleans, and enriches observations with astronomical features, trains stage-1 (detectability) and stage-2 (naked-eye vs. aided) models, selects operational thresholds, and validates externally against the Alrefay et al. (2018) published tables. The analysis scripts reproduce every table and figure of the accompanying paper, 'Sharjah criterion for lunar crescent visibility' (submitted to Astronomy and Computing).

creators.name: Talafha, Mohammed

notes: Changes in version 1.1.0: Moon lag times corrected (pipeline/03b_correct_moon_lag.py) and the model refitted; five-fold cross-validation grouped by lunation replaces the random 75/25 split; eight misread values (and two DAZ values) of the Alrefay et al. (2018) tables corrected; analysis scripts that reproduce the tables and figures of the paper added; new folder layout (pipeline/, analysis/, data/, models/, figures/, docs/); personal phone numbers in the ICOP report texts masked; outputs of the first version removed (they remain in version 1.0.0). Known issue: the 981 Monday reports lost to a date-parsing defect are still missing from crescent_features.csv.
